clue.text: Escape carrying whip and torch

indicators.note: one word carrying another holds it within itself, so the escape word surrounds the whip word

parts.note: a flight is an escape, as in taking flight
to lash is to whip; a lash is also the whip itself

explanation.surface: A fugitive makes a getaway clutching a whip and a torch, like an adventure-film hero.
explanation.definitionFit: In British English a torch is the portable battery lamp Americans call by this compound name.

clue.text: Fat? Radical to suppress pounds

indicators.note: to suppress is to hold down within, so the pounds sign is held inside

parts.note: radical and fab are both slang for excellent
L, from Latin libra, stands for pounds

explanation.surface: A dieting question: is a radical diet the way to cut pounds of fat?
explanation.definitionFit: Loose, excess body fat is called by this informal word.

clue.text: A rope, but not a second as well

indicators.note: not tells you to take out the letters for a and second

parts.note: a lasso is a rope with a noose
S is second

explanation.surface: Pick a rope, but don't take a second one too.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb meaning too, in addition, is a synonym of as well.

clue.text: Tough blighter regarding US city accepting source of corrupt cash

parts.note: hard means tough
a cur is a contemptible fellow, a blighter
re means regarding, about

indicators.note: the city takes in a letter

parts.note: NY is New York

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A hard-nosed rogue in New York takes a bribe.
explanation.definitionFit: Money from a stable economy, readily exchanged, is cash of a reliable kind.

clue.text: Current line in article from Frankfurt? One's not seriously engaged

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

indicators.note: the line letter goes in the German article

parts.note: der is the German masculine definite article
L is line

explanation.surface: A newspaper story from Frankfurt about electricity, read by someone not really paying attention.
explanation.definitionFit: A lazy person who does nothing in earnest is someone not seriously occupied.

clue.text: Try to tuck in after disease — a sign of life?

indicators.note: after places the eating word behind the disease, so it comes second

parts.note: a judge tries or hears a case
TB is tuberculosis
to tuck in is to eat heartily

explanation.surface: An invalid is urged to start eating after illness, a sign they're recovering.
explanation.definitionFit: A pulse or pumping of the heart is a vital sign that a person is alive.

clue.text: Repeat backing of Church House

indicators.note: backing means moving in reverse, so the church abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A church choir repeats its support for a particular house, perhaps a royal one.
explanation.definitionFit: A reverberation that sends a sound back is a repeat of it; the noun and verb both fit.

clue.text: Concern of film study — money provided by actors' union — ignoring European question

parts.note: to con is to study, as in conning a text
tin is old slang for money

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving out the letters for European and question

parts.note: Equity is the British actors' trade union
E is European
Q is question

explanation.surface: A film studies course funded by the performers' union, leaving out European questions.
explanation.definitionFit: Film crews track consistency between shots, so props and costumes match from take to take.

clue.text: Writers in Old English having identical magic phrase

indicators.note: the writers go inside the language abbreviation

parts.note: OE is Old English
pens are writing tools
the same means identical

explanation.surface: Scholars working in Anglo-Saxon share a spell.
explanation.definitionFit: Ali Baba's password that opens the robbers' cave is a famous magical formula.

clue.text: Neighbour of 22 almost entirely enthralled by a European

indicators.note: something enthralled is held captive, so the shortened word is held inside the European

parts.note: an Austrian is a European

indicators.note: almost the whole word, so its final letter goes

parts.note: all, as in 'all alone', means entirely

explanation.surface: Someone from next door, thoroughly captivated by a Continental visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 22 is KIWI, a New Zealander, so the definition points across the Tasman Sea; 'a European' is one nationality, not just the letter E.
explanation.definitionFit: Australians are the nearest national neighbours of New Zealanders across the Tasman Sea.

clue.text: This joint, mostly twisted, would lead to wail

indicators.note: twisted means turned about, and mostly says only the larger part, the last three letters, is turned, leaving the first letter where it stands

parts.note: to keen is to wail in lament for the dead

explanation.surface: A sore joint, badly twisted, would make anyone howl.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is written from the answer's side: twist most of this joint and it would become a wail. Keening is the Irish tradition of wailing for the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: The hinge joint between thigh and shin is a common example of a joint in the body.

clue.text: But the one at LSE won't be the cheapest available!

definitions.text: But the one at LSE won't be the cheapest available!

parts.words: But the one at LSE won't be the cheapest available!
parts.note: the London School of Economics teaches a class in economics

explanation.walkthrough: LSE is the London School of Economics, where a class in economics is one of these, though nothing at a top university comes cheap.
explanation.definitionFit: The cheapest cabin on a plane carries this name, played here against a lesson on economics.

clue.text: Actress upset about start of play with constant sources of alarm

indicators.note: the scrambled actress letters go round the other pieces
upset means knocked into disorder, so the letters of actress are rearranged

parts.note: Act I is the opening of a play
C is the usual symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light

explanation.surface: A rattled performer at the opening of a show, faced with endless frights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' scrambles the actress into SCARETS, and 'about' wraps that round the rest, which slips in before its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Intimidation methods meant to frighten people into compliance are deliberate sources of alarm.

clue.text: Black marks about points exhibiting vulgarity

indicators.note: the black marks go about, around, the points

parts.note: smuts are flecks of soot
tines are the points of a fork or antler

explanation.surface: Sooty specks on a fork's prongs show coarse behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene or indecent content is a form of coarseness, so the quality is vulgarity.

clue.text: I'm set to apprehend a bad lot initially allowing no opposition

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe dropped

indicators.note: to apprehend is to seize, so the setting word takes hold of the other letters

parts.note: to place is to set down

indicators.note: the first letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: A police officer resolves to arrest a gang of villains, brooking no resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unappeasable and relentless cannot be talked round or stopped, so permits no opposition.

clue.text: Significant symbol, trimmed at edges, encapsulating a city after revolution

indicators.note: encapsulating means enclosing, so the trimmed symbol holds the turned city
the first and last letters of the symbol word are cut away

parts.note: an emblem is a symbol

indicators.note: a revolution is a turning round, so these letters are read backwards

parts.note: Rome, the Italian capital

explanation.surface: A meaningful badge, its border clipped, contains a capital following an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trimmed at edges' leaves MBLE; 'after revolution' turns A ROME into EMORA, which goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something notable or worth remembering is significant; the adjectives are close synonyms.

clue.text: Plan example of 13?

definitions.meaning: a technical drawing or detailed scheme

explanation.walkthrough: Blue in British slang means indecent, as in blue jokes or films, so a blue print is an example of smut.
explanation.definitionFit: An architect's detailed design drawing is a plan, and by extension any detailed scheme.

clue.text: Lad taken aback about French article and other parts of speech

indicators.note: the reversed boy goes about, that is around, the French word
aback means backwards, so the word for lad is reversed

parts.note: a son is a lad, a boy
un is the French masculine indefinite article

explanation.surface: A boy is startled by a French grammar point and other bits of language.
explanation.definitionFit: Naming words for persons, places and things are a class of parts of speech beside articles.

clue.text: Lines produced during Tuesday will provide material

indicators.note: during puts the lines within the day

parts.note: L is line, so LL is lines

explanation.surface: A factory's Tuesday production lines will turn out some cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine net fabric used for veils and ballet skirts is a type of material.

clue.text: Mutual manoeuvring about period not concluding? This fixes an endpoint

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about, around, the shortened period
manoeuvring means moving pieces around, so the letters of mutual are rearranged
the period word loses its last letter

parts.note: a period is a time

explanation.surface: Two sides jockey over an open-ended period until one of them sets a deadline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvring' rearranges the first word into ULATUM, which goes about the shortened period; the definition is a cryptic description rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A final demand with a deadline sets the point after which negotiation ends, fixing where things stop.

clue.text: Take careful steps with stunt about to block reasonable location for lighthouse

parts.note: to inch is to move forward slowly and carefully
a caper is a prank or stunt

indicators.note: the abbreviation for about goes in and blocks the middle of the word for reasonable

parts.note: OK means acceptable, reasonable
C is circa, about

explanation.surface: A climber edges carefully along, performing a stunt to reach a sensible spot for a beacon.
explanation.walkthrough: The Inchcape Rock, off the east coast of Scotland, carries the Bell Rock lighthouse and is the subject of a Southey ballad.
explanation.definitionFit: This reef in the North Sea is where the famous Bell Rock lighthouse was built, so it is such a location.

clue.text: Most of circuit taking in English and French city

indicators.note: taking in means holding inside, so the shortened circuit holds the letter
all but the last letter of the circuit word

parts.note: a round is a circuit, as on a golf course
E is English

explanation.surface: A tour of most of the track with English and French cities on the way.
explanation.definitionFit: This Normandy city on the Seine, where Joan of Arc was burned, is a French city.

clue.text: Resident of islands keeping in with islanders initially

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: An islander gets on well with neighbours, keeping in with them.
explanation.definitionFit: New Zealanders, from an island nation, are nicknamed after their flightless national bird.

clue.text: Craze always involves such keenness

indicators.note: involves means contains, so the two words contain the answer

explanation.surface: A passing fad always brings with it this sort of enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: Fervour or eager enthusiasm for a cause is a strong form of keenness.

clue.text: Feel Berlin is home to … not this river

indicators.note: the two words house the answer among their letters

explanation.surface: A traveller senses Berlin has a famous waterway, but not the one you'd guess.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's point is true: Berlin lies on the Spree, not on this river, though the phrase 'Feel Berlin' houses it.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a major German waterway flowing through Dresden and Hamburg to the North Sea.

clue.text: Symbolic fruit offering better health, clearing cold

parts.note: a fig is a fruit

indicators.note: clearing means getting rid of, so the cold letter is taken out

parts.note: a curative remedy heals
C is cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A piece of fruit is a healthy remedy, curing a cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Language used in a non-literal, metaphorical way is symbolic rather than literal.

clue.text: Stop special police retreating

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police

explanation.surface: An order to halt as special police units pull back.
explanation.definitionFit: To staunch a flow of blood or a tide of complaints is to stop it.

clue.text: Consequence of strike action, say: refuses to sit and work

parts.note: someone who refuses to sit stands
to till is to work the soil

explanation.surface: A striker on the picket line won't sit down and won't work.
explanation.definitionFit: A strike brings production to a complete halt, the 'say' showing it is one example.
